title: LinearPredictorBFGS.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of f(x)=h(Ax), where h is convex and has an Lh-Lipschitz gradient. The condition Lh‖A‖²≤L makes f L-smooth. Neither h nor f is required to be strongly convex.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: A query (x,v) returns (α,∇f(x+αv)). In particular, v=0 supplies ∇f(x) exactly. Gradient correctness holds for every history and seed; there is no gradient error.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Bundled Armijo–weak-Wolfe line-search oracle: for descent directions, α>0, f(x+αv)≤f(x)+c1 α⟨∇f(x),v⟩ and ⟨∇f(x+αv),v⟩≥c2⟨∇f(x),v⟩. Each bundled reply costs one call; internal line-search evaluations are not separately counted. No function value is returned. Step choices may depend on history and jointly distributed seeds, without independence assumptions.

distinctive_assumptions.label: quadratic_growth
distinctive_assumptions.details: There exists a minimizer x* with ‖x0−x*‖≤R such that μ‖Ax−Ax*‖²/2≤f(x)−f(x*) whenever f(x)≤f(x0). Growth is measured in prediction space, and A may be rank deficient. Parameters satisfy 0<μ≤Lh and R≥0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The optimization and prediction spaces are Euclidean spaces ℝ^d and ℝ^m with their standard inner-product norms.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public information consists of d, m, x0 and L>0. Lh, μ, c1, c2, R and ε are hidden parameters, with 0<c1<c2<1 and ε>0; A and h are instance data. The allowed algorithm family is the supplied BFGS scheme initialized with cI for some c>0 selected from public information.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/LinearPredictorBFGS.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.allowedAlgorithm; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point must satisfy f(output)−f(x*)≤ε for a global minimizer x*. The supplied algorithm returns its current iterate after the fixed oracle budget, including its initial gradient query.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/LinearPredictorBFGS.lean: spec.successful, bfgs.output; supplied extracted budget; LongTails/Template.lean: execute.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee holds almost surely under the joint execution law. The oracle seed sequence may have arbitrary dependence.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: This is a structured smooth convex problem with prediction-space quadratic growth, a bundled unit-cost Armijo–Wolfe oracle, hidden line-search parameters, and an explicit BFGS-family restriction.

descriptionHtml:
BFGS for Linear Predictors

We consider BFGS for minimizing f(x)=h(Ax) on Rd, where A:Rd→Rm is linear and h:Rm→R is convex with Lipschitz gradient. A given starting point x0 lies within distance R≥0 of a global minimizer x⋆, and the objective gap controls squared prediction distance on the initial sublevel set. The oracle returns a step length and the exact gradient at the resulting point, satisfying Armijo–Wolfe conditions for descent directions. For ε>0, the goal is a last iterate x¯ satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the oracle’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Rdf(x). Here d,m∈N0, both spaces carry their Euclidean inner products and norms, and ∥A∥op denotes the induced operator norm. The parameters satisfy 0<μ≤Lh,L>0,0<c1<c2<1,R≥0,ε>0. The algorithm receives only d,m,x0,L; the parameters Lh,μ,c1,c2,R,ε may enter the oracle-call budget but are not algorithm inputs.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and smoothness). The function h is differentiable everywhere, and for every z,w∈Rm and t∈[0,1], h((1−t)z+tw)≤(1−t)h(z)+th(w),∥∇h(z)−∇h(w)∥≤Lh∥z−w∥. The linear map satisfies Lh∥A∥op2≤L.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance and prediction growth). There exists x⋆∈Rd such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈Rd,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R. For every x∈Rd with f(x)≤f(x0), μ2∥Ax−Ax⋆∥2≤f(x)−f(x⋆).

Assumption 3 (Armijo–Wolfe oracle). A query is any pair (x,v)∈Rd×Rd. The oracle returns (α,g)∈R×Rd with g=∇f(x+αv). Whenever ⟨∇f(x),v⟩<0, the reply also satisfies α>0,f(x+αv)≤f(x)+c1α⟨∇f(x),v⟩,⟨g,v⟩≥c2⟨∇f(x),v⟩. These conditions hold for every query, every prior query–reply history, and every realization of the oracle randomness. Replies may depend on the history and may be dependent across calls.

The task is algorithm-specific: we analyze BFGS with a scalar initial Hessian approximation. The algorithm chooses c>0 using only its available inputs and initializes B0=cId at the given point x0. One initial query (x0,0) supplies g0=∇f(x0); its step-length reply is discarded. For k≥0, the method queries (xk,vk), receives (αk,gk+1), and updates vk=−Bk−1gk,sk=αkvk,xk+1=xk+sk,yk=gk+1−gk,Bk+1=Bk−(Bksk)(Bksk)TskTBksk+ykykTykTsk. To define the recurrence also in singular cases, a scalar reciprocal at zero is taken to be zero, and the inverse of a singular matrix is the zero matrix.

After the initial query and K∈N0 updates, the output is the last iterate x¯=xK, using K+1 oracle calls in total. With zero calls, the output is x0. The required accuracy is f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s.

theorems.referencesHtml:
• Yu. E. Nesterov. A method of solving a convex programming problem with convergence rate O(1/k²). 1983. Complexity: O(1+LR2/ε) exact-gradient oracle calls for f(xN)−f∗≤ε, using accelerated gradient with known L and no function-value evaluations.
  • Amir Beck and Marc Teboulle. A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems. 2009. Complexity: O(1+LR2/ε) exact-gradient oracle calls for f(xN)−f∗≤ε, using constant-step FISTA with zero nonsmooth term and known L.

comparisonHtml:
f(x)=h(Ax) on Rd, with linear A:Rd→Rm, convex Lh-smooth h, L≥Lh∥A∥2, L>0, and 0<μ≤Lh. A minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and μ2∥A(x−x⋆)∥2≤f(x)−f(x⋆) whenever f(x)≤f(x0). The setup restricts algorithms to BFGS with positive scalar initialization; (1) uses B0=LI. The oracle returns an Armijo–weak-Wolfe step and its endpoint gradient, with 0<c1<c2<1. Target: f(xK)−f(x⋆)≤ε, ε>0, for every admissible oracle history. Bundled line-search calls include initialization; internal search trials have no stated gradient/value-call budget.

BFGS for linear-predictor objectives: LinearPredictorBFGS.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) LinearPredictorBFGS (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(1+κ3/2γ−3/2LR2/ε) line-search calls.
(2) BFGS (Ding et al. 2026, Thm. 3.1, Eq. (11)) O(1+LW02γε) line-search calls; B0=LI, W0<∞. (1): Distance-only BFGS bound, independent of design conditioning; ε−1/2 instead of ε−1. For W0≍R, total gain when LR2/ε≫κ3/γ. No uniform W0 bound in setup parameters: h(z)=∥z∥2/2, A=diag(1,δ), x0=(R,0) give W0≥R/(2δ). (1) needs composite growth; (2) covers general convex smooth objectives with finite W0. For W0≍R, (1) loses at coarse accuracy and has worse γ dependence.
(3) AGD/FISTA (Beck and Teboulle 2009, Thm. 4.4), fixed step, ψ=0 O(1+LR2/ε) gradient calls, available through v=0 queries; applies throughout the target objective class. (1) matches the ε−1/2 order for BFGS, with extra parameter factors; no problem-class complexity improvement. (1) pays κ3/2γ−3/2 and a larger leading constant; needs composite growth and line-search access instead of gradients alone.

Abbr: κ=Lh/μ; γ=c1(1−c2); f⋆=f(x⋆); X⋆=argminf; W0=supx∉X⋆,f(x)≤f(x0)(f(x)−f⋆)/∥∇f(x)∥; ψ is the FISTA nonsmooth term; δ>0 is a design singular value; ≍ means equality up to universal factors; ≫ means asymptotically larger.

source:
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.NonsingularInverse
import LongTails.Template

open Set Matrix
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.LinearPredictorBFGS

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Space (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)

structure Public where
  d : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  x0 : Space d
  L : ℝ

structure Params extends Public where
  Lh : ℝ
  μ : ℝ
  c1 : ℝ
  c2 : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  A : Space p.d →L[ℝ] Space p.m
  h : Space p.m → ℝ

def objective {p : Public} (I : Instance p) (x : Space p.d) : ℝ := I.h (I.A x)

noncomputable def bfgsUpdate {d : ℕ} (B : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) (s y : Fin d → ℝ) :
    Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ :=
  B - (s ⬝ᵥ (B *ᵥ s))⁻¹ • vecMulVec (B *ᵥ s) (B *ᵥ s) + (y ⬝ᵥ s)⁻¹ • vecMulVec y y

noncomputable def direction {d : ℕ} (B : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) (g : Space d) : Space d :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (-(B⁻¹ *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp g))

structure State (d : ℕ) where
  x : Space d
  g : Space d
  B : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ
  started : Bool

noncomputable def bfgs {d : ℕ} (c : ℝ) (x0 : Space d) :
    Algorithm (Space d × Space d) (ℝ × Space d) (Space d) where
  State := State d
  initial _ := ⟨x0, 0, c • 1, false⟩
  query st := (0, (st.x, if st.started then direction st.B st.g else 0))
  update st r :=
    if st.started then
      ⟨st.x + r.1 • direction st.B st.g, r.2,
        bfgsUpdate st.B (WithLp.ofLp (r.1 • direction st.B st.g)) (WithLp.ofLp (r.2 - st.g)), true⟩
    else ⟨st.x, r.2, st.B, true⟩
  output st := st.x

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := Space p.d × Space p.d
  Reply p := ℝ × Space p.d
  Output p := Space p.d
  publicInput := Params.toPublic
  valid q := 0 < q.μ ∧ q.μ ≤ q.Lh ∧ 0 < q.c1 ∧ q.c1 < q.c2 ∧ q.c2 < 1 ∧ 0 < q.L ∧
    0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q I oracle :=
    ConvexOn ℝ univ I.h ∧
    (∃ gradH : Space q.m → Space q.m, (∀ z, HasGradientAt I.h (gradH z) z) ∧
      ∀ z w, ‖gradH z - gradH w‖ ≤ q.Lh * ‖z - w‖) ∧
    q.Lh * ‖I.A‖ ^ 2 ≤ q.L ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn (objective I) univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧
      ∀ x, objective I x ≤ objective I q.x0 →
        q.μ / 2 * ‖I.A x - I.A xstar‖ ^ 2 ≤ objective I x - objective I xstar) ∧
    (∀ k seed x v, HasGradientAt (objective I) (oracle.answer k (0, (x, v)) seed).2
      (x + (oracle.answer k (0, (x, v)) seed).1 • v)) ∧
    (∀ k seed x v, ⟪gradient (objective I) x, v⟫ < 0 →
      0 < (oracle.answer k (0, (x, v)) seed).1 ∧
      objective I (x + (oracle.answer k (0, (x, v)) seed).1 • v) ≤
        objective I x + q.c1 * (oracle.answer k (0, (x, v)) seed).1 *
          ⟪gradient (objective I) x, v⟫ ∧
      q.c2 * ⟪gradient (objective I) x, v⟫ ≤ ⟪(oracle.answer k (0, (x, v)) seed).2, v⟫)
  successful q I output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn (objective I) univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), objective I (output ω) - objective I xstar ≤ q.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p algorithm := ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ algorithm = bfgs c p.x0

end LongTails.Setups.LinearPredictorBFGS
